To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the abstract semantics and structure of multidimensional ontological knowledge can be represented in Datalog with constraints, (ii) the grounding of multidimensional ontolgies is possible by using Datalog rules and constraints, and (iii) the grounding of ontologies in Data Warehouses can be done in a way that allows for efficient query answering.

(1) Datalog with negations can serve as a foundation to represent hierarchical and multidimensional ontology models, and (2) Datalog with constraints can be used to reason about multidimensional ontologies and to ground them in Data Warehouses.

(1) we propose hierarchical and multdimensional ontologies as an expressive formalism to capture the semantics of business terms and to support the reuse, maintainability, and understandability of OLAP queries, (2) we define the structure and semantics of hierarchical and multidimensional ontology in terms of Datalog rules and constraints, and (3) we discuss the grounding of hierarchical and multidimentional ontologies in the Data Warehouse as the fundament of the query formulation process.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design, formalization, implementation, and reasoning of multidimensional ontol- ogies.
a new approach to OLAP where multidimensional ontologies are used to define the conceptual layer in between business analysts and Data Warehousing.
the development of a new generation of OLAP engines that are able to support business analysts by providing a more flexible and more expressive conceptualization of multidimensional data.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
we have shown how to represent and reason with hierarchical and multidimensional concepts and how to use these concepts to query multidimensional data.
the paper provides a solid foundation for future research on Ontology-based OLAp.
the paper provides a solid theoretical basis to reason with multidimensional ontologies in the context of Data Warehouses.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we provide an ontology-based approach to OLAP that is based on Datalog and thus can benefit from existing Datalog-based reasoning techniques.
we show how to use Datalog-based reasoning over multidimentional ontologies as the basis of Ontology-based Data Warehousing.
we have developed a framework for Ontology-based OLAp that is based on a formal semantics and is implementable in a standard Datalog engine.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the use of Datalog with negations enables a very natural representation of multidimensional ontological knowledge and allows for the integration of ontological reasoning and Data Warehouse technology.

the combination of Datalog-based reasoning and the expressivity of multidimensional ontological models enables us to capture the semantics of business analysts in a way that allows for a better understandability, reuse, as well as a maintainability of their analytical queries.
Datalog with negations can be used to define the abstract semantics and structure of ontologies, which can be grounded in Data Warehouses.
